name: Checkout Field Visibility for eCommerce
author: zamartz

sections.description:
Checkout Field Visibility for eCommerce hides the billing and shipping fields your shop does not need, such as the company or the second address line, with no code.

What the free plugin does:

  • One rule set for billing fields and one for shipping fields.
  • Each rule set hides any of: first name, last name, email address, phone number, company, address lines 1 and 2, country, state or region, city and postal code.
  • Each rule set can have an order total condition (less than, greater than, less than or equal to, greater than or equal to, or equal to an amount), or no condition, so it is always used.
  • Works on the classic (shortcode) checkout and on the Checkout block. A hidden field is also removed when the order is placed, not only hidden on the page.
  • Settings under WooCommerce > Settings > Billing and WooCommerce > Settings > Shipping > Shipping Field Visibility, and the same settings under ZAMARTZ > Settings > Plugins. Administrators and WooCommerce Shop Managers can change them.

Paid add-on

A separate paid add-on, from zamartz.com, adds:

  • More rule sets for each section, with a priority and “Stop other rules”.
  • More conditions: order subtotal, shipping amount, tax amount, customer roles, products, product variations, product categories and coupons.
  • Making fields required or optional.
  • Hiding the whole billing or shipping section on the Checkout block.
  • Hiding the terms and conditions box, hiding or requiring “Create an account”, and requiring the customer to be signed in.
  • Messages shown at checkout when a rule set applies.
  • Import from the older WooCommerce Hide Billing Fields plugin.

The free plugin works fully without it.

What this plugin sends

Nothing, unless the site owner says yes to “Share anonymous events for ZAMARTZ plugins” (asked once in the admin, and changed any time under ZAMARTZ > Settings > General). With a yes, it sends an anonymous event to zamartz.com when the plugin is activated, deactivated (with the reason picked, if any) or deleted: the plugin’s name, the event, and a one-way code made from the site’s address (not the address itself). No email, user, order or shop data is sent. With the same yes, the ZAMARTZ dashboard loads news from zamartz.com once a day.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate WooCommerce.
  2. Install this plugin from Plugins > Add New, or upload the plugin folder to /wp-content/plugins/, and activate it.
  3. Go to WooCommerce > Settings > Billing (or WooCommerce > Settings > Shipping > Shipping Field Visibility), turn on “Hide billing fields” (or “Hide shipping fields”), tick the fields to hide, choose a condition if you want one, and save.
sections.faq:
What is in the free plugin?

One billing rule set and one shipping rule set, each hiding any fields, with an order total condition or none, on both checkouts.

What does the paid add-on add?

See “Paid add-on” above, and the product page.

Does it work with the Checkout block?

Yes. The Checkout block uses one field setup for its billing and shipping forms. When a field is hidden in one form only, the plugin hides it there with a small script and empties it on the server when the order is placed.

How do I remove the dashboard ads?

They are not shown on sites with an active paid add-on license, and each box can be closed.
sections.changelog:
4.0.0

The paid features move to a separate paid add-on. Your rule sets and your license are kept.

  • Changed: the paid features (more rule sets, the conditions other than the order total, required fields, hiding a whole section, the terms, create account and signed-in rules, messages, import, the search results setting and the network screen) moved to the paid add-on from zamartz.com. A site with a license installs the add-on to keep them; the license carries over with nothing to enter again. Nothing paid became free and nothing free became paid.
  • Changed: “Stop other rules” (paid add-on) now ends the checking only when its own rule set applies. In 2.0.0 a rule set with “Stop other rules” that did not apply also stopped every rule set after it.
  • New: the free rule set’s order total condition works, as this readme always said. In 2.0.0 the free plugin could not save a condition and applied its rule set to every order. A rule set saved by the free 2.0.0 has no condition and keeps applying to every order.
  • New: the settings are in WooCommerce’s settings and in ZAMARTZ > Settings > Plugins, one set of settings in two places. The WooCommerce tabs now show even while a section is switched off, because its switch is there.
  • New: WooCommerce Shop Managers can change the rule sets. The ZAMARTZ General tab stays administrators only.
  • Fixed: “Hide the terms and conditions” stayed on for every later customer once one order matched.
  • Fixed: every WooCommerce notice (other plugins’ included) was cleared each time an order was placed.
  • Fixed: a message was cut at its first apostrophe when saved (“We don’t ship” became “We don”).
  • Fixed: on the Checkout block a billing rule also hid or required the shipping field (and the other way round), and the rules were barely checked on the server. Each section’s rules now apply to its own form and are enforced when the order is placed.
  • Fixed: on the Checkout block, hiding a field WooCommerce requires (such as Last name or Postal code) no longer makes the order fail with “is required”. Hiding a field in billing only keeps the shipping field required, and the other way round.
  • Fixed: on the Checkout block, a field a rule hid when the page loaded never came back when a coupon (or a quantity, shipping method or address change) stopped the rule from applying, and the order then failed with “is required”. The rules now follow the cart while the shopper is on the page: fields are hidden and shown again at once.
  • Fixed: on the classic checkout the same change left the fields as they were drawn (as in 2.0.0); the checkout page now reloads when the rules for the cart change.
  • Fixed: an amount such as “19,99” was read as 1999; it is now 19.99 (“1,000” is still 1000).
  • Fixed: the settings save could write any option whose name contained the plugin’s prefix, and any option at all through a special name. It now saves only the section’s own settings.
  • Fixed: the settings save and every admin request now check the user’s permission and a security code.
  • Fixed: a translated “Free” label could switch the free plugin’s checks off.
  • Fixed: uninstalling deleted nothing (the option prefix was added twice). It now deletes the plugin’s own settings, its rule sets included; it never deletes the license or the paid add-on’s settings. Deleting the paid add-on removes the license and the add-on’s own settings, never a setting of this plugin.
  • Fixed: messages were printed more than once and into the checkout’s own updates on the classic checkout; they now show once above the form.
  • Fixed: a field another plugin put first in the billing or shipping fields stopped the rules for that section.
  • Fixed: PHP 8 warnings (properties created on the fly, FILTER_SANITIZE_STRING).
  • Removed: the plugin’s own copies of the usage events; the shared ZAMARTZ admin sends them, only with the site owner’s yes, without waiting for an answer.
  • Requires WordPress 7.0, PHP 7.4 and WooCommerce 11.3. Tested up to WordPress 7.1 and WooCommerce 11.3. Declares support for order storage in custom tables and the Checkout block.

2.0.0

  • NEW: WooCommerce Checkout Blocks support (first major blocks release)
  • NEW: Shared rules engine for classic and block checkout
  • NEW: Block checkout field hide/required via country locale and Store API validation
  • NEW: Block checkout support for hiding billing/shipping sections, terms, create account, and logged-in requirements
  • NEW: Ruleset messages display in the Store Notices block when placed on checkout
  • NEW: All qualifying ruleset messages can display when multiple rules match (paid)
  • NEW: Admin option to disable entire billing/shipping section on block checkout
  • IMPROVED: Order total and subtotal condition semantics aligned with WooCommerce cart totals
  • IMPROVED: Coupon matching supports coupon codes and legacy IDs

1.5.0

  • Updated accepted product IDs
  • Improved order total validation

1.4.0

  • Security fix: patched a path traversal problem in the admin settings
  • Improved input validation for admin settings tabs

1.0.0

  • First version, replacing the legacy plugin WooCommerce Hide Billing Fields.
